# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and widely supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, Git, CA certificates, and Open MPI
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    gfortran \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments, especially on cloud platforms like AWS
# This allows running as root, specifies TCP for communication over the primary network interface (eth0),
# and disables hardware-specific transports that may not be available.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=^openib
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1

# Clone, build, and install the amg2023 application
# The source code is cloned to a temporary directory.
# FIX: Build prerequisite libraries in the correct order before building the final executable.
# The executable is then copied to a system path, and the source code is removed.
RUN git clone https://github.com/LLNL/AMG.git /opt/amg2023 \
    && cd /opt/amg2023 \
    && make -C utilities \
    && make -C seq_mv \
    && make -C IJ_mv \
    && make -C krylov \
    && make -C parcsr_mv \
    && make -C parcsr_ls \
    && make -C test \
    && cp test/amg /usr/local/bin/amg \
    && cd / \
    && rm -rf /opt/amg2023

# Set a default command to show the application's help message
CMD ["amg", "-help"]

    && cp amg /usr/local/bin/amg \
    && cd / \
    && rm -rf /opt/amg2023

CMD ["amg", "-help"]

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the AMG2023 benchmark
# on a single Kubernetes node within an AWS CPU instance environment.
# It uses the Flux Operator to manage the parallel execution.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: amg-problem2-test
  # The namespace where this MiniCluster will be deployed. Omitted to use 'default'.
  # namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster. A size of 1 means all tasks run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run.
  # This will run 4 processes on the single pod.
  tasks: 4

  # When set to false, the MiniCluster pods and associated data are not deleted after the job completes.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs and results.
  cleanup: false

  # Settings for Flux logging behavior.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict checking of Flux configurations and operations.
    strict: true

  # Defines the container(s) that will run as part of the Flux job.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will prepend 'flux run -n <tasks> ...' to this command.
      # This runs AMG with problem type 2 and a small 4x4x4 grid.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4

      # Indicates that this container is a worker, not a pod responsible for launching the job.
      launcher: false

      # Ensures that the Flux broker and workers are started within this container.
      runFlux: true

context.optimize:
Maximize the amg2023 figure of merit. Start with -n 32 32 32 -P

and find optimal node resources. Then SLOWLY increase the problem size, one dimension at a time, by a small percentage to try to increase the FOM. The size of the MiniCluster MUST be 1. Tasks MUST be at least 4. To change the parameters you can multiply out 3 -P coordinates by 3 -n parameters and multiple by 64 bits to get a global problem size. The global problem size must fit in memory across nodes, in this case, just one. If you go over it will OOM. The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there.
